title: Adder circuits (half, full, ripple, lookahead)
summary: Adders are combinational circuits for binary addition. Half adder: sum = A XOR B, carry = A AND B. Full adder: sum = A XOR B XOR Cin, carry = (A AND B) OR (Cin AND (A XOR B)). Ripple carry adder: chains full adders (carry propagates, O(n) delay). Carry lookahead adder (CLA): computes carry in parallel using generate (G = A AND B) and propagate (P = A XOR B) signals, O(log n) delay.

structure.meaning: Sum = A XOR B. Carry = A AND B. No carry input.
Sum = A XOR B XOR Cin. Carry = (A AND B) OR (Cin AND (A XOR B)).
Chain n full adders. Carry out of bit i feeds carry in of bit i+1. Delay = O(n) (carry ripples through all bits).
Generate: G_i = A_i AND B_i. Propagate: P_i = A_i XOR B_i. Carry: C_{i+1} = G_i OR (P_i AND C_i). Parallel computation of all carries. Delay = O(log n).
Compute both possible sums (with carry 0 and carry 1) for each block, then select based on actual carry. Faster than ripple, slower than CLA.
Tree-based carry computation. Delay = O(log n). Used in high-performance CPUs.

notes: Half adder uses 1 XOR + 1 AND gate (5 transistors in CMOS).
Full adder uses 2 XOR + 2 AND + 1 OR (or 9 NAND gates).
Ripple carry adder is simple but slow (n * gate delay).
CLA is used in most modern ALUs for speed.
Addition is the basis of subtraction (two's complement), multiplication (shift and add), and division.
